metadata.case_name: HO WAI-YEE v. YIP CHUEN AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: laboratory technician, employed by the Hong Kong Government in the Department of Health

injuries.description: (a) internal bleeding and removal of her spleen;
source: (a) internal bleeding and removal of her spleen;

injuries.description: X-ray examination revealed fractures to the plaintiff's ninth and tenth ribs
source: X-ray examination revealed fractures to the plaintiff's ninth and tenth ribs, as well as a comminuted fracture of her left shoulder blade.

injuries.description: a comminuted fracture of her left shoulder blade
source: X-ray examination revealed fractures to the plaintiff's ninth and tenth ribs, as well as a comminuted fracture of her left shoulder blade.

injuries.description: (c) scars of varying intensity to seven sites over her body.
injuries.body_part: abdomen; left chest; scalp (back of head); right temple; left elbow; right thumb; left foot
source: (c) scars of varying intensity to seven sites over her body.

manifestations.description: She was knocked unconscious and woke up in the Accident and Emergency Department of Queen Elizabeth Hospital.
required emergency treatment for life threatening internal injuries.
The removal of her spleen has caused the plaintiff distress and discomfort, insofar as she has been far more prone to cold symptoms and she has suffered diarrhoea far more often since the accident.
rib injuries are known to be extremely painful
pain, discomfort and inconvenience for at least three years after the accident
The scar down her abdomen is large and unsightly
she is unable to wear midriff revealing clothes such as a bikini or a halter top

The scalp scar to the back of the head is just as prominent now as in the photograph. The plaintiff can cover it with certain hairstyles but is conscious of it whenever she bends forward, for example, before colleagues in the office. Further, she feels slight pain and some discomfort there whenever she brushes her hair
The right temple scar ... it is often itchy "as if bitten by ants". She must always wear her hair in the same style to cover this scar.

The left elbow scar is still quite nasty in that there is still a small and hard purple coloured lump present. Her consciousness of this scar causes her to always wear clothing that will cover it so that, for example, short-sleeved T-shirts or tops are out of the question.
The right thumb scar is still as prominent as in the photograph. Although it is now well healed, it is still shiny in appearance.
The left foot scar is "not a problem" to the plaintiff.
permanent, unsightly scars with a cosmetic disability of 8 per cent

treatments_received: operation to transfer a large flap of skin and hair from the back of her scalp to the site of the defect at her right temple area
pressure garment therapy (elasticated T-shirt, elasticated glove on right hand, wrap-around tube on left elbow worn 24 hours a day for three years)
treatments_future: further operation to improve abdominal scar (proposed by Dr MA)

losses.description: Indignity and embarrassment of the scars for the rest of her life; unable to wear midriff revealing clothes; must always wear hair to cover scars; conscious of scars and avoiding short-sleeved tops.
Interference with the plaintiff's immune system following splenectomy resulting in being far more prone to cold symptoms and suffering diarrhoea far more often since the accident.
